clue.text: Ex-footballer went wrong, driving over South African mountain with Ford rep?

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to go wrong morally is to sin
berg is the Afrikaans-derived South African word for a mountain, as in the Drakensberg
the Ka is a small Ford car
a Member of Parliament represents a constituency

explanation.surface: A former player has gone off the rails, driving a Ford over a mountain in South Africa with a sales rep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' just places the first piece in front of the mountain. 'Ford rep' looks like a car salesman but splits into a Ford model and a parliamentary representative.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch striker starred for Arsenal and has long since retired from playing, so he is a former footballer.

clue.text: Display joy skywards, some light filling the void

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading skywards means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
something filling a space sits inside it, surrounded on both sides
a void word has been emptied of its middle, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of this short word
the lux is the SI unit of illumination, so a measure of light

explanation.surface: Someone lifts their joy to the heavens as light pours into an empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: The light unit goes inside the emptied article, and the whole thing is then read upwards to give EXULT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice openly and triumphantly, which is showing happiness for others to see.

clue.text: Formidable article underpinning Cockney residence in news

indicators.note: to underpin is to support from beneath, so in a down entry this goes at the bottom

parts.note: the first letter of the word, which itself spells out the compass points
a Cockney drops the H of home
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a fearsome piece beneath a story about a Cockney's house.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'underpinning' puts the article at the bottom. Cockney speech drops the initial H, so a home becomes 'OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something no mean feat or no mean player is an idiom for saying it is impressive and considerable.

clue.text: Date set for gig featuring this?

definitions.text: Date set for gig featuring this?

parts.note: a squeeze is informal for a boyfriend or girlfriend, someone you date
the box is slang for the television set

explanation.surface: A booking diary entry: the date is fixed for a gig starring this instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an instrument a gig might feature; read in parts, a romantic partner plus a TV set build the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze-box is an accordion or concertina, an instrument often heard at folk gigs.

clue.text: Genuine groove, with tango at end

indicators.note: placing a letter at the end means it is attached last, after everything else

parts.note: to etch is to cut a groove; its own T is removed to be relocated
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A real groove, rounded off with a tango at the finish, like a dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The groove word already contains a T; that tango is shifted to the end, turning ETCH into ECHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword in English meaning authentic or real, used of typical, true examples.

clue.text: Where to work out mounting beer habit

parts.note: a gym is where people exercise

indicators.note: mounting means climbing upwards, which in a down entry reads bottom to top

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager

explanation.surface: Advice on where to burn off a growing beer-drinking habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like an addiction but is clothing, as in a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment, and a gymslip is the sleeveless pinafore dress once worn as British school uniform.

clue.text: Travel on water with amp, as smoother

parts.note: A is the symbol for amp
qua is Latin-derived for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
a plane is a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood

explanation.surface: Gliding over water with an amplifier aboard, used to smooth things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' belongs to the definition, though it tempts you to look for AQUA in the wordplay; the little word 'as' supplies QUA.
explanation.definitionFit: To aquaplane is to ride a board towed over the surface, or to skid along on a film of liquid.

clue.text: Dick previously right leaving somewhat criminal firm

indicators.note: a letter that is leaving departs from the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: pretty means fairly or somewhat
R is the abbreviation for right; it is the letter removed
a con is a convict
stable means firm and steady

explanation.surface: A detective once quit a firm that was rather crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' is slang for a detective, and 'previously' marks the term as historical. 'Somewhat criminal' looks like a phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty constable was a parish officer keeping the peace in former times, so a lawman of the past.

clue.text: Cool old Mod promoted vogue wee singer

parts.note: calm and unruffled
O is a standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, and in a down entry going up reverses the letters

parts.note: taken as written
in vogue means in fashion
to go is a euphemism for to urinate

explanation.surface: A cool old Mod is pushed as the fashionable little singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like the Scottish 'small' qualifying the singer, but it is a call of nature. A Mod was a 1960s British youth-culture stylist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish tenor is one of the Three Tenors, famous for opera performances worldwide.

clue.text: Exhibitionist's forte, for all to see, in light aircraft

parts.note: forte is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: being in something means enclosed by it

parts.note: the de Havilland Moth was a light aircraft
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A show-off's speciality is flying a light plane in full view of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For all to see' sounds like display, fitting the show-off, but it is the film-rating letter; the Tiger Moth is a classic biplane.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudmouth is a person who talks noisily to draw attention, much as an attention-seeker shows off.

clue.text: Get bull's eye in test? Tom might do

indicators.note: being in something means enclosed by it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles

indicators.note: the eye of something is its centre, as in the eye of a storm

parts.note: the two central letters of the animal

explanation.surface: Hit the bullseye in a darts test, which a chap called Tom might manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is not a person but a male cat. The bullseye of darts is a red herring: the 'eye' takes the centre of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats shed their fur seasonally, and a tom, being a male cat, can lose its coat that way.

clue.text: Company drinking nothing with mature type of cheese

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for company
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A firm that avoids alcohol pairs its meals with a mature cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' tempts you towards cheddar, but it is a verb meaning to grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage cheese is a soft, lumpy fresh curd cheese, one of the recognised varieties.

clue.text: Fail to go along with vacuous party disc

parts.note: to flop is to fail

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is cleared out

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Refusing to go along with a dull party record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disc' looks like a party record but is the old computer storage medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy is a short name for the flexible magnetic disk once used to store computer files.

clue.text: Country's Ulez extremists head around south disrupting equipment

indicators.note: extremists are those at the extremes, so the end letters

parts.note: Ulez is London's Ultra Low Emission Zone; its outer letters

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it on all sides

parts.note: bean is slang for the head

indicators.note: something disrupting another breaks into it, ending up inside

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Activists who oppose London's clean-air zone lead a protest, breaking equipment in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers, one nested in the other. Ulez is London's Ultra Low Emission Zone, a charge on polluting cars that stirred angry protests.
explanation.definitionFit: Uzbekistan is a nation in Central Asia, formerly part of the Soviet Union.

clue.text: I've made a mistake keeping last of ruminant does from those over the hill

definitions.text: does from those over the hill

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: D'oh! is Homer Simpson's exclamation on realising an error

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone admits a blunder in keeping deer, the female animals coming from beyond the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like female deer, fitting the ruminant, but is the verb. 'Those over the hill' are old folk, so the old form of the word is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Doth is the archaic third-person form of 'do', as used in older English and the King James Bible.

clue.text: Asian fly semi-visible circling polished sink

indicators.note: circling something means surrounding it on all sides
if only half is visible, just half of the word is kept

parts.note: the tsetse is an African fly; only its first half is kept
A1 means first-rate, perfect, and is written here as AI
to wane is to decline or sink

explanation.surface: An insect from the East, half seen, circles a gleaming sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polished' in the sense of first-rate supplies A1, with the digit read as the letter I. 'Sink' looks like a basin to be polished but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Taiwan, an island state in East Asia, is Taiwanese, so the word describes an Asian person.

clue.text: Rather soft police like this reported one that's hammered?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police; 'so' means like this
a piano's strings are struck by felt hammers

explanation.surface: Gentle policing like this is said to belong to someone who's drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' looks like drunk, but it describes an instrument whose strings are hit by hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mezzo-piano is the musical direction meaning moderately quiet, played a little louder than piano.

clue.text: Servant, most senior member, switching variable exercises

indicators.note: switching one algebraic unknown for another swaps a single letter in the word

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day
the doyen is the senior member of a group

explanation.surface: A servant, the eldest of the staff, varies their exercise routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Y and Z are both letters used as variables in algebra, so one replaces the other in DOYEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily dozen is a set of physical workouts done each morning to stay fit.

clue.text: Increasingly hot year, one in July etc going topless

indicators.note: being in something means enclosed by it
going without a top means losing the first letter

parts.note: the abbreviation for year
July and its neighbours are the summer months
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Each year gets hotter, and in July someone goes topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like temperature, fitting the summer, but means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummy is slang for sexy or attractive, and the comparative describes someone growing more so.

clue.text: Stream second musical band

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid or gas
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Streaming a band's second album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical band' suggests a pop group, but here it is a gang in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jets are the rival street gang to the Sharks in West Side Story, a band of youths in a musical.

clue.text: Gun lifted, repeating shock

indicators.note: lifted means raised up, and in a down entry going up reads backwards

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mop of it
repeating supplies a second copy of the same piece

explanation.surface: A gun is raised, delivering one shock after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' suggests a jolt, but means a thick head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The pom-pom was a quick-firing automatic cannon, especially used as an anti-aircraft weapon.

clue.text: Hum fast track like master

parts.note: the M1 motorway, read as letters
as means like
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Humming along as fast as a master would.
explanation.walkthrough: A hum is British slang for a bad smell. The M1 is England's main north-south motorway, a fast road written with a one that reads as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant or unhealthy vapour, so a foul smell hanging in the air.

clue.text: Islanders here regularly view local clothing James reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so letters are trimmed away
clothing something wraps around it
doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the two words
Jim is a shortened form of James

explanation.surface: People on an island here regularly see locals wearing James's cut-down clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every second letter across both words, not just one. The definition works by pointing to the place where islanders live.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima is a small Japanese volcanic island, famous for a Second World War battle, so where islanders are found.

clue.text: Contemporary preserver of language

definitions.note: the answer names the people's tongue, used as a noun

parts.note: in means fashionable, current
a tin can preserves food

explanation.surface: A modern guardian of a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserver' suggests a person keeping a tongue alive, but it is the food tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Quechua, spoken in the Inca empire of the Andes, is the Incan tongue, so the word names a form of speech.

clue.text: Spam perhaps behind topping in fridge

parts.note: a bum is the behind or backside

indicators.note: the topping is what sits on top, so the first letter in a down entry

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tinned Spam lurking at the back of the fridge, maybe on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spam' looks like the tinned meat, fitting the fridge, but is junk email. Bumf is British slang for useless paperwork or junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk email is unwanted reading material, an example of the useless paperwork and junk the slang term covers.

clue.text: Detective annoyed, recalling hiding spots

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run backwards
words hiding something conceal it within their letters

parts.note: found spanning the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An irritated detective remembers the places where things were concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: Detective first suggests DI and annoyed a synonym, but the letters run backwards across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi are birthmarks or moles, coloured marks on the skin.

clue.text: Two-thirds of chocolate bar magpie left out there

indicators.note: taking two of three parts means a third is cut off

parts.note: Bounty is a coconut chocolate bar; its last four letters
Pica is the magpie's genus name
the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A magpie made off with part of a chocolate bar left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out there' looks like a location but means unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out there is weird or unconventional, so it is not representative of the norm.

clue.text: Excessive nicety about punishment guys received in public

indicators.note: something received in a place is taken inside it

parts.note: overt means open, done in public view
re means about, concerning
a fine is a monetary penalty
guys are men

explanation.surface: Fussing too much over the punishment the men got in front of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In public' looks like where the punishment happened, but it supplies the outer word that receives the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-refinement is taking subtle distinctions or polish too far, a fussy precision beyond what is needed.
